r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')

print((p/'manuscript.txt').read_text()[:30000])

strengths: Significance: Accelerating repeated MIP solves is practically useful. PreMIO requires only predicted binary values and additional cardinality constraints, making integration with commercial solvers straightforward. Solving all four complementary regions preserves exhaustive coverage independently of prediction quality.
Originality: Interpreting separate cardinality budgets for predicted zeros and ones through concentration inequalities is a potentially useful perspective on designing learned search neighborhoods.

Empirical promise: Experiments cover knapsack, set covering, and an SCUC application model using two commercial solvers and several heuristic settings. Figure 1 reports substantial primal time-to-target improvements, while Table 1 suggests more modest gains for complete search.

Presentation, limitations, and ethics: The main pipeline and Algorithm 1 are understandable. Remark 6 explicitly acknowledges unrealistic posterior assumptions, and Section 4.4 discusses infeasible restrictions. These disclosures are valuable. The described public and synthetic datasets raise no apparent material research-ethics concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness—central coverage guarantee: Theorem 2 applies marginal correctness probabilities to U and L, although these sets are selected from predictions on the same test instance. A3 does not justify transferring marginal accuracy or independence to these selected subsets. For example, independent, rare false positives can yield high overall accuracy while every selected positive is incorrect. Appendix B.4 therefore does not establish the claimed high-probability inclusion of an optimal solution.

Soundness—independence and the practical model: Appendix B.1, equation (4), incorrectly factors an expectation over the shared test instance into a product of expectations. Independent training datasets do not imply independent errors on that instance; the additional appeal to non-overlapping feature segments is neither an established assumption nor sufficient without further independence conditions. Theorem 3's conditional Hoeffding argument also needs conditional independence of solution variables, whereas A6 concerns predictions. No calibration or dependence assessment bridges these assumptions to the fitted logistic models, and some SCP training labels are obtained with a 10% optimality-gap tolerance.

Soundness—pruning: Section 3.2 states that complementary branches become infeasible when the preferred region excludes all global optima. This is false: a complementary region then contains a better solution satisfying the proposed objective cutoff. Even when the preferred region contains an optimum, the cutoff need not make complementary LP relaxations infeasible. The general suggestion of nearly free certification is insufficiently supported.

Evaluation: Section 4.4 excludes instances with infeasible PreMIO restrictions or mutual timeouts, reducing 132 instances to 57. Consequently, the reported 16% improvement is conditional on outcome-dependent selection and does not establish performance over the original benchmark without failure and fallback accounting. Section 4.2's targets are chosen from PreMIO's own achieved objectives; this useful time-to-target measure needs complementary fixed-budget objective/gap comparisons and explicit handling of targets the baseline never reaches.

Originality and significance: The mechanism is closely related to prediction-distance constraints in Ding et al. [11] and local branching [12], but evaluation compares only against the underlying solvers. Comparisons with these approaches and ablations against fixed or validation-tuned cardinality radii are missing. Thus, the benefit attributable specifically to the concentration-based design remains unclear.

Reproducibility: Although hardware, basic generators, and sample counts are supplied, the manuscript provides no code/data availability statement, exact experimental solver versions, random seeds, detailed logistic-regression fitting procedure, or training/inference cost accounting. SCUC has only five test instances per configuration, without uncertainty estimates. Table 3 lists only 30 entries, including a duplicated blp-ar98, despite the claimed 57-instance evaluation.

Presentation affecting implementation: Appendix D defines alpha_L and alpha_U as misclassification rates but calls them accuracies and proposes maximizing them. It also recommends tau approximately 0.1 despite specifying tau in [0.5, 1). These inconsistencies directly affect constraint construction and prevent an unambiguous implementation of the advertised tuning procedure.
